name: io.github.beepboop2025/seiche
title: Seiche: World-markets evidence terminal
description: Money, FX, capital-market and metadata-only China macro evidence with source clocks and limits.

tools.name: source_rights_status
tools.description: List the research tools available in this release, the one legacy reading shown research only (Funding Pop, in money_market_context), and the legacy features withheld pending source qualification. Returns policy and source-rights metadata only; does not grant redistribution rights or certify freshness.

tools.name: gift_city_context
tools.description: Read dated USD/INR funding, separate ECB and CBUAE VAT FX references, and CFTC COMEX gold positioning. Cache-only research with source clocks; no executable prices or regulatory eligibility determination.

tools.name: gold_inventory_carry
tools.description: Calculate fine gold, simple financing cost and INR per fine gram from explicit decimal-string assumptions. All inputs are caller supplied, no quote is verified, and inputs are not persisted.

tools.name: market_workbench
tools.description: Query dated observations for a selected currency pair and optional accepted China annual series. Choose this for a time series, same-date FX cross, or observed-interval change; use world_markets_context for a chartless overview and money_market_context for funding-desk metrics. Read cached official FX reference histories and same-date currency crosses, with native units, provenance, age and observed-interval changes. Inspect owner-accepted Palimpsest China annual economic series and revision-aware history beside the CNY reference. Daily fixings, annual context and licensed gaps remain distinct. No collection, model fitting, executable quotes or scoring.

provider.description: Official FX reference source. Both currencies must be supported by this provider; the response lists its currencies.

base.description: Base currency: each returned value is quote-currency units per one base unit. Must differ from quote.

quote.description: Quote currency for the selected pair's dated history; must be supported by provider and differ from base.

days.description: Calendar-day FX lookback from today, not an observation count. Only cached observations on shared dates are returned; gaps are not filled.

china_series.description: Optional exact cn.wdi.* identifier from the response's china.series catalog. Omit to select the first accepted series, if available; never invent an ID or infer withheld values.

tools.name: research_network
tools.description: Discover which published datasets and sibling-product tools can answer a research question. Choose this for catalog discovery and handoff links, not for market observations: use world_markets_context for a market overview or market_workbench for supported FX and China histories. Explore the Palimpsest dataset catalog by topic, with source clocks, rights, freshness and pagination. Includes Seiche's separately completed funding context and explicit research steps into institution filings, exit liquidity and NarcoScope's granular global data. Source metadata and funding interpretations stay distinct. May fetch the published catalog; does not retrieve underlying dataset values or call the suggested sibling tools. No source collection, score changes, causal joins or trading authority.

topic.description: Research topic used to filter dataset metadata and select suggested sibling-product tools. This does not query those tools or retrieve dataset values.

offset.description: Zero-based offset within the filtered catalog. Use the returned next_offset while keeping topic and limit unchanged.

limit.description: Maximum dataset metadata entries per page; suggested research steps are separate from this page size.

tools.name: money_market_context
tools.description: Inspect a funding desk's rates, spreads, policy corridor, liquidity buffers and source-level evidence. Choose this for detailed funding metrics; use world_markets_context for a cross-asset overview, or market_workbench for FX and accepted China time series. Start with section='summary' for USD; it also returns funding_pop, a separate research-only block with its skill, as the website shows it. Use section='countries' for the public-source country catalog, or add country='JP' (a supported ISO alpha-2 code; UK is an alias for GB) for dated policy, funding, liquidity and sovereign references. Country coverage is partial and monthly references are explicitly separate from daily curves. Granular, descriptive USD money-market context from the already assembled desk: policy corridor and overnight spreads; SOFR/TGCR/BGCR distributions and tails; repo-segment rates and volumes; CP-Treasury spreads; bills and cash curve; liquidity buffers and Fed facilities; and MMF repo plumbing. Use section='rates_catalog', 'funding_conditions', 'curve', 'spread' or 'rate_series' for the official rates research desk: stored series with source clocks; overnight benchmarks against policy anchor and corridor across currencies; government curves with slopes and exact forwards where the convention allows; spread percentiles in their own history with the window stated. Use section='india_states' for RBI's weekly state government securities (SDL) auctions by state (latest auction, 52-week issuance, cut-offs and bid cover). Use section='india' for the India funding, RBI liquidity, policy and sovereign-curve desk from a bounded canonical observation read. It keeps benchmark identities, date alignment, curve movements and mechanism hypotheses separate. India defaults to view='full' for compatibility; prefer view='summary' for findings, constraints and an exact metric ID catalog, then view='metric' with metric_id for one complete evidence card. These India-only views are independent reads, not a pinned snapshot or pagination. Otherwise use optional `section` to request a compact summary, one named USD desk section, diagnostics, sources, methodology, or all context. Diagnostics count funding persistence, compare secured/unsecured benchmarks and show calendar cohorts with sample limits, without changing any score. Returns exact-date alignment, native-cadence changes, empirical own-history statistics, freshness, coverage, formulas, sources, and caveats as applicable. Chart history is always omitted. USD reads only an already completed cached or persisted snapshot; it never triggers collection or engine recomputation, while freshness is re-evaluated at response time. Context only: no causal, predictive, probability, or trade claim.

section.description: Projection to return; defaults to the compact desk summary.

country.description: Country code for section=countries only. Omit to list supported countries; UK aliases GB.

view.description: India only: legacy full desk, compact findings/catalog, or one exact metric card.

metric_id.description: Exact ID from the India summary metric_catalog; required only for view=metric.

markets.description: funding_conditions only: comma list of market ids, for example US-USD,EA-EUR.

window_days.description: funding_conditions and spread only: own-history window in days for percentiles.

curve.description: curve only: curve id, for example EA_AAA_SPOT. Omit to list curves.

date.description: curve only: ISO date; the latest curve date on or before it is used.

compare.description: curve only: comparison ISO date, same rule as date.

spread.description: spread only: spread id, for example EA_AAA_2S10S. Omit to list spreads.

instrument.description: rate_series only: instrument id from section=rates_catalog.

tools.name: world_markets_context
tools.description: Summarize the available money-market, FX, macro-capital and China evidence when a question spans markets or its scope is not yet clear. Start with section='summary', then select a relevant section. For detailed funding metrics use money_market_context; for dated FX/accepted China observations use market_workbench; for external dataset discovery use research_network. This chartless overview is not a time-series query. It projects only completed/public state into money_markets, forex, macro-capital transmission, China macro evidence, official references, methodology, or a compact summary. Every response carries snapshot/as-of clocks, canonical Seiche citation URLs, and explicit observed, derived, structural, restricted, and unavailable boundaries. The China structural catalog is unsigned; only status=restricted represents a verified Seiche owner-attested revision; both states keep NBS values, raw evidence, and history withheld. A separately operator-accepted economic_context may publish licensed World Bank WDI values with annual/structural freshness, distinct release, Palimpsest collection, and Seiche acceptance clocks. Those values are context only and never a live print, score, gauge, forecast, or signal. The sources selector is reference-only; use all when verified China context and its NBS source linkage must appear together. Coverage is curated and partial rather than exhaustive or uniformly live. It never triggers collection, repository history reads, or model fitting. Its named-field whitelist omits chart and history arrays for data minimization; that is not a per-record licensing audit. Capital coverage is limited to public positioning proxies, Treasury primary-market absorption, market stress, official liquidity and global dollar credit—not a security master, issuer-data service or consolidated tape. Executable depth, liquidity-provider concentration, and position-sized exit costs are outside this tool's scope.

section.description: Projection to return; defaults to the compact cross-market summary.

tools.name: data_health
tools.description: Freshness, provenance, and fault status for every underlying series (FRED, NY Fed, OFR, Treasury). Call this to confirm the board is current before relying on a reading.
